title: Change
description: One change to a character, from the fixed set of change types (kept in sync with `data/change-types.json`). applyChanges takes a batch and applies all of it or none of it. A change failing this schema is a shape error; one that fails against the character and ruleset is a runtime error.

adjust.description: Adjust a numeric input field (a counter) by an amount. Tags (`damage.fire`) let incoming-change effects such as resistance modify the amount first. `faces` are die faces for the dice its incoming-change effects roll; applyChanges writes them in when it rolls, so a logged adjust replays without rolling. `situational` holds the receiving player's situational choices for it.

faces.description: Die faces for the incoming-change effects' dice `add`s, consumed in order as they are rolled. Faces left over are `faces-mismatch`; too few, with no dice function, `faces-required`.

situational.description: The receiving player's situational choices for this change, by qualified ID: a reaction such as Uncanny Dodge. Each selected choice (a boolean that's true, another value that isn't its default) must be offered (`available`) and its `incoming` must match the change (`situational-unavailable`); its incoming-change effects then apply while this change is routed, and not to its overflow or the rest of the batch. An action never sets it.

addItem.description: Add a copy of a content item to the inventory (carried types) or features.

entry.description: A copy's instance ID, or an applied entry's: its keys and bounds are those its source's content type and item declare.

value.description: The new value; with `copies` or `applied`, a formula evaluated per copy or entry (an action has already replaced any `steps`, `flags` or `params` in it with literals).

path.description: A pick, with `option`: the choice it is in, as `choose` names it. Its keys and bounds are those the picked content declares (its content type's and its own).

grant.description: With `entry` (a copy) or `path` and `option` (a pick): the content that node's holder grants name, by qualified ID, whose saved state changes (the node's `grants`). It must be active there (`not-granted`). Its keys and bounds are those the granted content declares; a value equal to its default (the grant's `state` value, else the declared default) is dropped.

not.description: `grant` names a grant on a copy or a pick only.

entry.description: A copy's instance ID, or an applied entry's: its keys and bounds are those its source's content type and item declare.

by.description: The amount; with `copies` or `applied`, a formula evaluated per copy or entry (an action has already replaced any `steps`, `flags` or `params` in it with literals).

path.description: A pick, with `option`: the choice it is in, as `choose` names it. Its keys and bounds are those the picked content declares (its content type's and its own).

grant.description: With `entry` (a copy) or `path` and `option` (a pick): the content that node's holder grants name, by qualified ID, whose saved state changes (the node's `grants`). It must be active there (`not-granted`). Its keys and bounds are those the granted content declares; a value equal to its default (the grant's `state` value, else the declared default) is dropped.

not.description: `grant` names a grant on a copy or a pick only.

setField.description: Set a copy's own value of an item field its content type marks `perCopy` (`key`, the field's name), saved in the entry's `fields`; `null` removes it, so the item's value (or its templates') applies again. Checked as `setState` is: a field that isn't `perCopy` is `not-per-copy`, a value of another type `wrong-type`, an `id` or `set` member naming no content or field `unknown-id`.

value.description: The new value, or `null` to remove it; with `copies`, a formula evaluated per copy.

setQuantity.description: Set a copy's `quantity`. It may not be below 0 (`out-of-range`); a copy at 0 stays.

value.description: The new quantity, an integer; with `copies`, a formula evaluated per copy (an action has already replaced any `steps`, `flags` or `params` in it with literals).

adjustQuantity.description: Add `by` to a copy's `quantity`. The result may not be below 0 (`out-of-range`); a copy at 0 stays.

by.description: The amount, an integer; with `copies`, a formula evaluated per copy (an action has already replaced any `steps`, `flags` or `params` in it with literals).

template.description: Apply a template to, or remove it from, a copy of an item.

applyEffect.description: Apply content to the character: an `applied` entry. Without `id`, applyChanges gives the entry `<source local id, dots as hyphens>-<n>`, the smallest n >= 1 that no copy, applied entry or earlier change in the batch uses.

state.description: The entry's state. A value may be `{ formula }`, a formula an action passed on because it reads `batch`: applyChanges evaluates it with `item` the source's item, this character's fields and `batch`, and the change as applied (`changes` in the result) carries the value.

removeEffect.description: An applied entry by its instance ID, or applied entries by query (`applied`).

toggleEffect.description: Set `active` on an applied entry, by its instance ID, or on applied entries by query (`applied`).

choose.description: Pick an option (choose). Un-picking (unchoose) is `#/$defs/unchoose`. A choice a grant presets takes neither (`preset-choice`).

unchoose.description: Un-pick an option (unchoose), removing its nested picks in the same all-or-nothing change. Without `option`, every pick of the choice is removed with its nested picks; a choice with none is left unchanged (not `not-picked`).

choicePath.description: Where a choice lives: on an entry (or the character's rules-level choices when `entry` is absent), then alternating choice IDs and picked options down to the choice. `["martial-archetype", "5e-srd-5.1:subclasses.champion", "additional-fighting-style"]`.

setExtension.description: Replace one app's extension data. `value: null` removes it.

finishCreation.description: Finish creating the character: clears `creating`. Rejected with `creation-incomplete` while the character, with the batch's earlier changes applied, has rules issues or pending choices; the error's `data.issues` lists them, pending choices as `too-few-picks`. On a character that isn't being created it does nothing. A creation action proposes it as its last change, so applying the action's changes is the player's confirmation; a character made by hand finishes the same way.

setHomebrew.description: Replace the character's own homebrew; `homebrew: null` removes it. Rejected with `homebrew-error` when the new homebrew doesn't load, and with `unknown-id` while the rest of the file still names homebrew content or fields it no longer has. Later changes in the batch see the new homebrew; a batch whose first change is setHomebrew doesn't load the old one. Actions can't propose it.

dismissFollowUp.description: Dismiss an ephemeral follow-up: delete the character's stored follow-up with this `id` (as computeSheet's `offers` gives it) without acting on it. A required one too: `required` is advisory. A derived offer can't be dismissed: it lasts exactly as long as its condition holds. An ID with no stored entry is `unknown-follow-up`.

clearFollowUp.description: Clear an ephemeral follow-up that was acted on: delete the character's stored follow-up with this `id`. No entry with the ID is no change, so applying an action's changes after another app cleared it still works. startAction proposes it last when it runs a stored follow-up's action (`action.followUp`), and the `changes` computeSheet lists for a stored follow-up end with it.

offerFollowUp.description: Offer a follow-up: store the named follow-up of the character as an ephemeral offer, as if it had fired, once the batch is applied. Proposed by an action (a step's or option's changes, or changes content adds to a step) to name what may come after it: a sorcerer's blood magic after a cast. `followUp` and `source` name the declaration as a stored follow-up does; `params` are evaluated values that replace the declaration's own. The declaration's `when` and its action's availability are checked after the batch, as for a triggered follow-up; one the character doesn't have then, or a derived (`while`) one, isn't stored. A follow-up no loaded pack declares is `unknown-follow-up`.

followUp.description: The follow-up's ID: `<pack>:<id>` for the rules', `<content or type qualified ID>#<id>` for content's.

source.description: For a follow-up on content: the content and copy declaring it, as computeSheet's sources name them.

params.description: Parameter values for the follow-up's action, replacing the declaration's own of the same name.

proposed.description: A change proposed by an action step. Same types as a change, but values may be formulas and `entry: self` means the copy making the action; the engine resolves them before returning. With `split`, one proposed adjust becomes one change per tag group (typed damage). An addItem's `entry` is an object whose values may be formulas. An applyEffect names its `source` with a formula and may leave out `id`; removeEffect, toggleEffect, setState and adjustState may name applied entries by query (`applied`). equip, applyTemplate and removeTemplate compute `equipped` and `template`; setExtension stays the app's. An offerFollowUp names a follow-up of the content or rules whose action, option or added changes propose it, with `params` as formulas.

type.description: Any change type but setHomebrew, dismissFollowUp and clearFollowUp.

when.description: The change is proposed only when this holds.

forEach.description: Propose the change once per element of this list, in list order, with `x` bound to the element. `when` and the change's other formulas are evaluated per element; an empty list proposes nothing. Each copy counts toward `maxActionSteps` (a follow-up's toward `maxFollowUps`). `x` is not bound in the formulas a change passes on.

pick.description: setState and adjustState: `self`, the pick whose content defines the running action, resolved to `path` and `option` in the returned change. In an action that isn't a picked content's, `unknown-reference`.

grant.description: setState and adjustState: `self`, the grant that activated the running action's granted content (a holder grant), resolved to `entry` (or `path` and `option`, a pick) and `grant` in the returned change. In an action that isn't a granted content's, `unknown-reference`.

field.description: set and adjust may compute it: `{ formula }`, evaluated when the action runs to a field ID and qualified against the action's pack, as a literal one is. For `to: self` or a role it must name an input field (`unknown-field` or `not-input-field`, data: `field`); for a link it must be qualified and is passed on unchecked. A `split` adjust's field is written out.

oneOf.description: An existing copy's instance ID, `self` (the copy making the action), or `picked` (in the `changes` of a choice step over copies: the picked copy).

value.description: Evaluated by the action, unless the change has `copies` (or `applied`) and this reads `self`, `item` or `batch`: then it is passed on for applyChanges to evaluate per copy, with each path rooted at `steps`, `flags`, `params` or `action` replaced by its value as a literal.

by.description: Evaluated by the action, unless the change has `copies` (or `applied`) and this reads `self`, `item` or `batch`: then it is passed on for applyChanges to evaluate per copy, with each path rooted at `steps`, `flags`, `params` or `action` replaced by its value as a literal.

split.description: adjust only: split this change by tag. The engine emits one adjust per distinct tag under `by` among the roll items of step `roll`, evaluating the change's `by` formula once per group with `part` bound (`part.total`, `part.tag`). Each emitted change carries the change's tags plus the group's tag; items with no tag under `by` form one more group carrying only the change's tags. Incoming-change effects (resistance) then apply to each change separately.

copies.description: setState, adjustState, setQuantity, adjustQuantity, equip and removeItem: the copies to change, by query, instead of `entry`. The type is qualified against the action's pack; `where` and per-copy formulas (those reading `self` or `item`) are passed on for applyChanges to evaluate per match, and other formulas are evaluated by the action. Formulas passed on may also read `steps`, `flags`, `params` and `action` (the action's own `item`, `self` and `step`), which the action replaces with their values as literals. They may read `batch`: the batch's earlier field adjustments on the receiving character.

where.description: Evaluated per candidate copy by applyChanges, with `item` and `self` bound to it. May also read `steps`, `flags`, `params` and `action` (`action.item`, `action.self`, `action.step`): the action replaces each path rooted there with its value as a literal, and `has()` of one with `true` or `false`, before passing the change on. A path to a map is `type-mismatch`.

applied.description: removeEffect, toggleEffect, setState and adjustState: the applied entries to change, by query, instead of `id` or `entry`. `where` and per-entry formulas (those reading `self` or `item`) are passed on for applyChanges to evaluate per entry, with `steps`, `flags`, `params` and `action` replaced by their values as literals, as for `copies`. `limit` is a literal integer >= 1.

path.description: choose and unchoose: the choice. `entry` is an instance ID, `self` or `picked` as for `entry`; without it the choice is a rules-level one. `choice` is the path as a list of literal segments, or a formula giving the list (`"['playbook', steps.playbook.picked, 'special-ability']"`).

option.description: choose and unchoose: a formula naming the option (`picked.id`). An unchoose may leave it out to remove every pick of the choice.

id.description: applyEffect: the new entry's instance ID (without it, applyChanges picks one); removeEffect and toggleEffect: the applied entry's.

source.description: applyEffect: a string formula naming the content to apply, qualified against the action's pack as a proposed addItem's `item` is. A source that names no content, or a template, is `unknown-reference` when the action runs; for a link, or a role or target when qualified with a pack the ruleset doesn't load, it is passed on as written.

active.description: applyEffect and toggleEffect: a boolean formula.

state.description: applyEffect: the entry's state, each value a formula of the key's type. A value that reads `batch` is passed on as `{ formula }`, with `steps`, `flags`, `params` and `action` replaced by their values, for applyChanges to evaluate with `item` the source's item, the receiving character's fields and `batch`.

equipped.description: equip: a boolean formula, evaluated by the action, for the copy `entry` names or every copy `copies` matches.

template.description: applyTemplate and removeTemplate: a string formula naming the template, qualified against the action's pack as `source` is. One that names no template is `unknown-reference` when the action runs; for a link, or a role or target when qualified with a pack the ruleset doesn't load, it is passed on as written.

followUp.description: offerFollowUp: the follow-up to offer, by its own ID: one declared by the content (or its content type) whose action proposes the change, or whose `changes` effect adds it to a step; in a rules action, a rules follow-up (local or qualified). The action resolves it to the qualified ID and the content's `source`, and always proposes the change to the actor, whatever the step's `to`. One the owner doesn't declare is `unknown-reference` when the action runs.

params.description: offerFollowUp: formulas for the follow-up's action parameters, evaluated by the action; a formula giving `null` leaves its parameter out.

allOf.description: A computed field is for set and adjust, and not with split.
offerFollowUp names its follow-up, and only it takes `followUp` and `params`.

computedEntry.description: An instance ID computed when the action runs: a string formula, such as `{ formula: params.weapon }`. It is passed on as evaluated, for a role, a target or a link as for the actor; the character receiving the change checks it as it would a written ID.

computedField.description: A field ID computed when the action runs: a string formula, such as `{ formula: x }` or `{ formula: params.skillA.id }`.

proposedEntry.description: addItem only: the copy to add. `item` is a string formula naming a content ID (a local ID is qualified against the action's pack); `quantity` is an integer formula, `equipped` a boolean formula, and each `state` value a formula of the key's type. Without `id`, the engine uses `<item local id, dots as hyphens>-<n>` with the smallest n >= 1 that the character and earlier changes of the same action don't use. In `choices`, a pick's `option` may be `{ formula }`, evaluated by the action (with `x` under `forEach`) to a string or number; the tree's keys stay literal. The picks are checked when applied, as a `choose` of each is.

proposedChoiceTree.description: A proposed addItem's picks: a character file's choice tree, but a pick's `option` may be `{ formula }`.

copies.description: Per-copy changes (setState, adjustState, setQuantity, adjustQuantity, equip, removeItem) may name their copies with a query instead of `entry`. applyChanges resolves it against the character it changes, at that point in the batch: the copies of `type` (inventory, then features, each in file order) whose `where` holds, with `item` and `self` bound (`steps`, `flags` and `params` are not names here: an action substitutes them before passing a change on). With `limit`, only the first that many match. In such a change, `by` and `value` are formulas evaluated per match with the same binding, and formulas resolve names in the content type's pack. No match is not an error.

limit.description: With `copies`: change at most this many matches.

picks.description: setState and adjustState may name picks by query: applyChanges resolves it against the character it changes, at that point in the batch: every pick, in file order (each copy's choice tree, then the rules-level one, depth first), whose picked content declares the change's `key` and whose `where` holds with `item` the picked item and `self` its state (with declared defaults). With `limit`, only the first that many. `by` and `value` are formulas evaluated per pick with the same binding. No match is not an error.

grants.description: setState and adjustState may name granted content by query: applyChanges resolves it against the character it changes, at that point in the batch: each active holder grant, in activation order (the same item on one node once), whose granted content declares the change's `key` and whose `where` holds with `item` the granted item and `self` its state (saved, else the grant's `state`, else declared defaults). With `limit`, only the first that many. `by` and `value` are formulas evaluated per grant with the same binding. No match is not an error.

applied.description: removeEffect, toggleEffect, setState and adjustState may name applied entries by query instead of `id` or `entry`. applyChanges resolves it against the character it changes, at that point in the batch: the `applied` entries, in file order, whose `where` holds with `item` the source's item and `self` the entry (`id` and its state, with declared defaults). With `limit`, only the first that many. In such a change, `by` and `value` are formulas evaluated per entry with the same binding, and formulas resolve names in the source's pack. No match is not an error: each such change adds `{ applied: [ids] }` to `adjustments`.
